title: Breaks, Shifts & Fakeouts
hook: Clear Break or Fake?, pass the Knowledge Check, and save your Check-In to unlock Section 6.

game.title: Break or Fake? 👀
game.doneBadge: Break or Fake?: all 8 levels cleared
game.doneLine: You checked which level broke, how it broke, and what it actually told you. And you didn’t let one wick or one red candle rewrite the story.

steps.text: Bullish structure. The relevant HH is marked.

options.label: Bullish BOS
options.why: A close through the relevant HH, with the bullish structure. Continuation information.

options.label: Bearish MSS
options.feedback: Price broke a high in a bullish structure. That’s with the structure.

options.label: Not a structural break
options.feedback: It closed through the relevant HH. That’s a meaningful break.

steps.text: New HH. A pullback. Now price closes above a tiny internal high.

options.label: Yes, it closed above a high
options.feedback: Only a tiny internal high broke. The new HH is still above price.

options.label: Not necessarily
options.why: Only the tiny internal high broke. The new HH hasn’t been closed through.

asks.hint: Which high did price actually close above? Is the new HH still above price?

levels.name: BOS or not?
levels.goal: Labels are on. Decide which breaks carry larger meaning.

debrief.showed: A close through the relevant HH (bullish BOS), then a close through a tiny internal high only.
debrief.why: The tiny internal high sat inside the pullback. The new HH, the level that would confirm larger continuation, was still above price.

steps.text: Bullish structure. Three lows are lettered. Watch price break them.
Price closed through A, then B, then C.

tap.prompt: Which break meaningfully challenged the prior structural progression? Tap it.
tap.hint: Which low did price launch from to make the HH?

notes.6: A formed inside the pullback. It’s internal.
notes.8: B also formed inside the pullback.

tap.why: C. It was the HL supporting the bullish progression.

asks.prompt: So the break of C is…

options.label: A potential bearish MSS: change information
options.why: Against the bullish progression, through the swing that supported it.

options.label: A bearish BOS
options.feedback: The structure was bullish. A break against it is change information, not continuation.

options.label: A signal to sell now
options.feedback: MSS is change information, not an entry.

levels.name: Find the MSS
levels.goal: Letters only now. Which break actually matters?

debrief.showed: A and B were internal lows inside the pullback. C was the HL supporting the bullish progression.
debrief.why: Only the close through C challenged the structure itself: a potential bearish MSS.

levels.name: Wick vs. close
levels.goal: Rapid fire. Where did the last candle’s body finish? Build the streak.

items.why: Close: the body finished beyond the level.
Wick: price visited beyond the level, then closed back inside.
Wick: price visited beyond the level, then closed back inside.
Close: the body finished beyond the level.
Wick: price visited beyond the level, then closed back inside.
Close: the body finished beyond the level.
Close: the body finished beyond the level.
Wick: price visited beyond the level, then closed back inside.
Wick: price visited beyond the level, then closed back inside.
Close: the body finished beyond the level.

debrief.showed: Some candles only visited beyond the level. Others closed beyond it.
debrief.why: A wick can visit. A close gives stronger confirmation that price finished beyond the level.

steps.text: Bearish structure. Two highs are lettered.
Price rallies and closes above B. A is still above price.

asks.prompt: Has the bearish structure necessarily reversed?

options.label: Yes, price rallied and broke a high
options.feedback: B was internal. The swing holding the bearish structure is still intact.

options.label: No
options.why: Price rallied and broke an internal high, but the relevant LH (A) is intact.

asks.hint: Which lettered high is the relevant LH? Has price closed through it?

asks.prompt: Which level would need to break to challenge the bearish structure?

options.label: A
options.why: A is the relevant LH supporting the bearish progression.

options.label: B
options.feedback: B already broke and the structure wasn’t challenged. It was internal.

levels.name: Continuation or pullback?
levels.goal: A rally inside bearish structure. Don’t let it rush you.

debrief.showed: An internal high (B) broke. The relevant LH (A) held.
debrief.why: A rally against the structure isn’t a reversal by itself. The swing supporting the bearish structure stayed intact.

levels.name: Retracement or reversal?
levels.goal: More context, fewer gifts. Read the supporting swing and what price built after it.

items.why: Deep pullback, but the supporting HL held and price turned back up. Possible retracement.
Still pulling back. The supporting HL hasn’t been tested and price hasn’t turned. Not enough information.
Closed through the supporting HL, then a lower high and a lower low. Potential reversal.
Price wicked through the supporting LH but closed back below it, then turned down. Possible retracement.
Closed through the supporting LH, then a higher low and a higher high. Potential reversal.
A bounce inside bearish structure. Nothing relevant has broken yet. Not enough information.

debrief.showed: Some pullbacks held the supporting swing. Some closed through it and built new structure. Some hadn’t shown enough yet.
debrief.why: Levels decide it, not candle color or the size of the move.

steps.text: A candle closes above the prior high.

options.label: Smart money trapped the breakout buyers
options.feedback: The chart can’t show who traded or why.

options.label: Price moved above the prior high and failed to hold above it
options.why: That’s exactly what the chart shows. False break behavior.

options.label: A bearish reversal is confirmed
options.feedback: Price returned below a level. That alone doesn’t confirm a reversal.

options.label: Price broke out
options.feedback: It closed above, then returned below. It didn’t hold.

levels.name: Fakeout
levels.goal: Describe what happened. Only what the chart shows.

debrief.showed: A close above the prior high, then two candles back below it.
debrief.why: Observation before interpretation. “Failed to hold above the level” is what you can see. Who did it, and why, isn’t on the chart.

steps.text: Bearish structure. The swing holding it is highlighted.

asks.prompt: Is the old swing still holding the bearish story?

options.label: Yes, I marked it
options.feedback: Price closed through it. A level isn’t important forever because you marked it.

options.label: No. It was invalidated
options.why: The old swing was closed through. The bearish story is materially challenged.

tap.prompt: Which swing matters now? Tap it.
tap.hint: Which swing is the new move building from?

notes.5: That low belongs to the old story.

tap.why: The new higher low. It’s the swing the new structure is building from.

levels.name: Update your structure
levels.goal: Your chart updates because price updates.
levels.readPrompt: Which swing matters now? Tap it.

debrief.showed: The old swing was closed through, then price built a higher low and a higher high.
debrief.why: Once a level is invalidated, its job in the old story is done. The new higher low is what the new structure is building from.

steps.text: No labels. You know what to look for.

options.label: Bullish
options.feedback: Look at the swings inside the pullback. Are the highs and lows getting lower?

options.label: Bearish
options.why: Lower highs and lower lows inside the pullback.

options.label: Nothing
options.feedback: There are swings inside this pullback. Compare them.

steps.text: A candle trades below the last internal low.

asks.prompt: Did price close through the external supporting swing?

options.label: Yes
options.feedback: Find the low that launched the big move up. Is price anywhere near closing below it?

options.label: No
options.why: A wick below an internal low. The external supporting swing is far below and untouched.

steps.text: Price rallies and closes above the external high.

options.label: The bullish structure reversed to bearish, then reversed back to bullish
options.feedback: The larger bullish structure was never invalidated. Its supporting swing wasn’t closed through.

options.label: Internal bearish movement developed inside the larger bullish range, but the larger relevant bullish structure was not confirmed invalidated before continuation resumed
options.why: Exactly. The furniture moved. The room didn’t. Then price continued.

options.label: A bearish MSS confirmed a reversal, and the reversal failed
options.feedback: No close through the external supporting swing means no larger MSS was confirmed.

options.label: Nothing happened. Price only went up
options.feedback: Internal structure did turn bearish for a while. That’s worth seeing.

levels.name: Final boss
levels.goal: No labels. No hints on the chart. Read the whole story.

debrief.showed: Internal bearish swings and a wick below an internal low, but no close through the external supporting swing. Then bullish continuation.
debrief.why: Internal structure can turn without invalidating the larger structure. Only a close through the relevant external swing would have challenged it.

questionBank.question: Bullish structure. Inside the latest pullback, price closes above a tiny internal high. The relevant HH is still above price. What happened?
options: A minor internal break. A larger BOS isn’t confirmed
questionBank.why: Before you label a break, identify the level. Only a tiny internal high broke.

questionBank.question: A candle trades below the previous candle’s low. No swing low is anywhere near. What broke?
questionBank.why: Just the last candle’s extreme. No swing broke.

questionBank.question: Your friend says, “Price broke a low, so it’s bearish now.” What should she ask first?
options: Which low broke, and did price close through it?
questionBank.why: Different lows carry different weight, and a wick isn’t a close.

questionBank.question: Bearish structure: LH → LL → LH. Price closes below the relevant prior LL. What is it?
questionBank.why: A close through the relevant low, with the bearish structure.

questionBank.question: Right after a bullish BOS, which statement is accurate?
options: Price just proved it progressed with the existing structure
questionBank.why: A BOS describes what price just proved, not what it will do.

questionBank.question: Bullish structure. Price closes through the HL that supported the latest HH. What does that give you?
options: A potential bearish MSS: change information
A confirmed reversal and a short entry
questionBank.why: A close through the supporting swing, against the bullish progression.

questionBank.question: A trader says, “MSS printed, so I’m entering now.” What’s the flaw?
options: MSS is change information that the structure may be transitioning, not an entry signal
She should wait for two MSS
questionBank.why: MSS does not mean enter immediately.

questionBank.question: Bullish structure, pulling back. An internal low broke. The supporting HL and the prior HH are both intact. Best read?
questionBank.why: Nothing relevant has broken in either direction. “I don’t know yet” is the honest read.

questionBank.question: Bearish structure. Price rallies and closes above an internal high, but the relevant LH holds. Has the bearish structure necessarily reversed?
options: Yes, if the candles were green
questionBank.why: An internal high broke. The swing supporting the bearish structure is intact.

questionBank.question: Price drops hard with six red candles but never closes through the supporting HL, then forms a new HL. Best description?
options: Possible retracement inside the bullish structure
questionBank.why: Size and color don’t decide it. The supporting HL held.

questionBank.question: Price closes through the supporting HL, then forms a lower high and closes below the new low. Best description?
questionBank.why: The supporting swing broke, and new bearish structure formed after it.

questionBank.question: A candle wicks above the relevant HH and closes back below it. What happened?
options: Price traded above the level but didn’t finish above it
questionBank.why: A wick can visit. It didn’t close there.

questionBank.question: In this framework, which carries more significance when judging whether a structural level actually broke?
options: A candle close through the level

questionBank.question: Resistance is 20,000. A candle closes at 20,005, then the next closes at 19,985. Most objective description?
options: Price moved above the level and failed to hold above it
questionBank.why: Describe what the chart shows: failed breakout / false break behavior.

questionBank.question: Which statement is an observation, not an assumption?
options: Price traded below the prior low and returned above it

questionBank.question: Price closes through the HL supporting your bullish story. What now?
After the bullish structure is invalidated, price forms a lower high and a lower low. Which swing is more relevant now?
options: The old HL that already broke
The first low on the chart
questionBank.why: Your chart updates because price updates.

Why does the swing being broken matter?
What’s the difference between a wick through and a candle close through?
Why isn’t every pullback a reversal?
